subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a dwarf blacksmith character, chunky and Warcraft-styled with pauldrons, braided beard, leather apron, hammer and glowing anvil, built using the SDK's builder, joint, chain, sweep, and part functions.

Now I'm working out the rig: hips as root, spine, neck, head, jaw, arms, and legs, with the dwarf facing +Z and positioned near an anvil on a stump. I'm setting a compact 1.45m height with short legs, wide chest, a large horned helmet head, and a readable pose where the right hand grips a hammer and the left holds tongs toward the anvil, then defining the spine chain points from hips up through chest.

Setting head radius and noting the beard will cover most of the lower face anyway. I'll add a separate jaw joint and box part positioned under the mouth, aimed forward, with the beard attached to it.

Now I'm defining the hips root joint and spine chain, then working out the leg joints — hip, knee, and ankle positions for each side, building them as a polyline chain with named joints.

Sweeping the leg geometry with tapering radii for a smooth rounded shape, then adding boot geometry: a dark leather box with toe cap, sole flush to the ground, and a cuff cylinder at the top, all anchored to the ankle joint. Now I'm starting on the arms, placing the shoulder joint and beginning to work out elbow and wrist positions for a thick dwarf arm.

I'm deciding to simplify the hands — using a sphere at the wrist with a basic box-and-thumb for fingers rather than full digit joints, to keep things manageable. Mirroring the arm across the body with a sign flip for left/right, I'm now positioning the right arm to hold a hammer, working out wrist placement and the handle's angle so the hammer head rests up and forward over an anvil.

Working out the hammer head orientation...

Now I'm positioning the left wrist holding tongs that reach toward the ingot on the anvil, working out the anvil height relative to the stump and dwarf's stance so the hammer arcs down to strike around z=0.6.

I'm sweeping the torso as a tube along the spine chain, tapering its width and depth from hips to chest, and giving it a tunic color with a flattened belly sphere for shape. Now I'm adding pauldron-style half-sphere shoulders onto the frame.

Working out head placement and proportions so the dwarf's helmet and horns fit within a sensible 1.4-1.6 unit height, then positioning the eyes on the face sphere using surface geometry calculations.

Now I'm figuring out the angry eyebrows -- tilted boxes positioned above the eyes, using rotation around the z-axis so the outer end lifts for a fierce expression, mirroring the angle depending on which side of the face it's on.

For the rest of the face, I'm adding a reddish bulbous nose, rosy cheek spheres, small pointed ears, a braided mustache made from curved shapes under the nose, and a thick beard built from stacked, flattened ellipsoid shapes that cascade down from the cheeks toward the chest.

Now I'm working out the beard's color and structure—ginger-toned hair tapering down the chest, with two side braids made of alternating small spheres capped by a gold ring, plus some cone-shaped tufts at the bottom for texture, positioned carefully so they sit just in front of the chest geometry without clipping.

Next I'm shaping the helmet as a lathed dome profile sitting atop the head, defining the curve points that round over the forehead and close back along the central axis, then positioning it to cover the top of the head just above where the eyes and brows will sit.

Tapering horns bone-colored with pointed caps, lowering tip height to keep proportions dwarf-like at roughly 1.65 total. I'm adding ginger hair as a sphere mass behind the head with a braid down the back, then starting the leather apron as a flat slab covering chest to knees.

Working out apron outline coordinates...

Still shaping the figure geometry...

Still building out the limbs and extremities... planning tunic sleeves with leather bracers on the forearms, then working out hand geometry—gripping fingers wrapped around the handle for one hand, an open palm with simple finger rods for the other, keeping joints minimal where possible.

Now I'm moving to the anvil setup: a wooden stump base with bark rings, then the anvil itself built from a foot, waist, and top face oriented along the x-axis, positioning the hammer arc and ingot height, and shaping the horn as a cone extending outward.

Checking the dwarf's proportions against the anvil height confirms waist-level work makes sense. Now I'm adding a glowing orange ingot box on the anvil with hotter yellow ends, then positioning tong rods running from the left wrist toward the ingot.

I'm scattering a dozen tiny glowing spark spheres near the ingot at randomized positions for visual flair, skipping extra forge props beyond the anvil to keep things simple. For the arms, I'm setting fixed shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions rather than using IK, with thick geometry and pauldrons hiding the joints, keeping the rest pose with arms extended and separated.

Now I'm working on the legs, adding boot straps and gold buckles instead of knee pads, then moving to the jaw with a hinge joint at the chin, a lower jaw box, and a hidden dark mouth slit mostly covered by facial hair. I'm starting to sculpt the mustache as curved capsule sweeps on each side using bezier control points.

For the beard, I'm stacking shaped spheres cascading down the chest with decreasing size, checking that it overlaps the torso front correctly, and planning drooping conical tufts at the ends.

Adding beard tufts and gold rings...

Now I'm planning braided beard strands with alternating gold beads and ties hanging at the sides, then deciding on the blacksmith's outfit—apron and pauldrons with gauntlets rather than full armor—plus a glowing rune emblem and a row of rivets along the apron's top edge.

Defining the color palette for skin, hair, tunic, leather, gold, steel, wood, and fire tones.

I'll keep things simple with flat color strings rather than metal paints, and set up small helper functions for creating body parts and ellipsoid shapes attached to bones.

Now I'm figuring out which skeleton joints to attach each body part to—mapping the chest, belly, belt, apron, and pauldrons to the appropriate spine, hip, and arm joints so everything sits in a sensible place.

Writing sweep and limb code...

Still placing boot details...

Now I'm moving to the arm sleeves, defining a bracer helper that computes direction from elbow to wrist and builds a steel cylinder segment along that vector.

Adding hands next: palm spheres with small knuckle spheres for fingers, plus leather gauntlet cuffs at the wrists, then starting the hammer's handle as a wood rod attached to the right wrist bone.

For the hammer head, I'm positioning a steel box centered along the handle's direction with larger striking-face caps at each end, though I'm wrestling with how to orient these caps correctly relative to the handle's axis -- considering whether to merge geometries or just place parts using local offsets instead.

The cleanest fix is treating the head's Part as its own frame: once I create the main head box as a Part, I can place child pieces using that frame's local coordinates with the same direction, so they automatically inherit the correct orientation without extra quaternion math. I'll apply this same local-frame technique for the rune/diamond details, anvil faces, spark effects, and the tapered stump cylinder near the base.

Now I'm laying out the anvil and stump geometry more precisely: tapered stump with root cones at the bottom, stacked anvil sections (base, waist, top body) at specific heights, plus a heel box and horn cone extending outward to complete the anvil silhouette.

I'm setting up the overall figure height and importing the glow effect kit, then establishing a seeded random function for consistent randomness. For the spark particles, I'm generating a batch of small octahedron/sphere shapes scattered around the forge area with randomized positions and sizes using the fire glow material.

I'm attaching the sparks to the root bone and defining the eye details with blue irises and glints, then estimating the total part count should land around 150-200. Moving on to facial features, I'm positioning the ears, cheeks, and nose with appropriate scale and skin-tone coloring for the dwarf character.

Now I'm adding sideburns to connect the beard with the head, then building the apron through an extrusion with a leather color, bevel, and bone attachment, making sure the outline points don't self-intersect, plus a darker hem band and pocket details.

Positioning the pocket box and rivets, then placing a gold diamond emblem on the apron chest area with a rotated box and darker inner detail. I'm checking the belly and apron geometry so the apron doesn't float away from the body at the hips, considering whether to tilt the apron or add a pelvis sphere to fill the gap.

Now I'm defining the arm skeleton chains for both sides, setting shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions mirrored left and right, parented to the chest/spine tip with named bone chains for the arm role.

I'm shaping the sleeve coloring with a tunic-to-skin gradient along the arm sweep, adjusting the radius taper from shoulder to wrist, and deciding a leather bracer at the color boundary is enough without adding a separate cuff ring.

Now I'm building the pauldron: a steel ellipsoid base with a thin gold-trimmed torus rim, a steel spike cone angled outward, and a second darker steel plate layered beneath it, all rigged to the shoulder joint bone, then wiring the head geometry to the neck's bone tip before writing the final strict TypeScript code.

I'm sweeping a bezier curve along the head bone to form a bone-colored horn with a flat start cap and pointed tip, adding a small gold sphere at the base as a decorative cap, and now sketching out a helper function to generate braided hair strands.

For the back pony braid, I'm positioning it from the top of the head down along the back, alternating hair-colored segments with shrinking radii, capping it with a gold ring and tufted cone tip, but I'm realizing the z-offset needs adjusting so the braid doesn't collide with the torso's back surface.

With the geometry settled, I'm finalizing the export with mirror loops and double-checking that imports from the SDK (THREE, createBuilder, polyline, catmull, bezier, lerp, rng) are all actually used. For the hammer's placement, I'm computing a normalized direction vector and positioning it relative to the wrist using Vector3 operations like addScaledVector, confirming both array and Vector3 inputs work for positions before writing the final code.
